full_judgment:
Mahfuzur Rahman, J: This Rule under section H 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and decree passed by Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong, in other Appeal No. 557 of 1984, remanding the case back for fresh trial setting aside the judgment and decree passed by Munsif, North Raozan, in other Suit No. 237 of 1983 on 30.5.1984 decreeing the suit. 

 4. The learned Munsiff, after trial, decreed the suit on contest against the contesting defendant No. 2 and ex-parte against the rest. The defendant No. 2 being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree preferred Other Appeal No. 557 of 1984. The learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Commercial Court, Chittagong, who heard the appeal, by his judgment and decree dated 16.3.1986 allowed the appeal on contest without cost setting aside the judgment and decree of the Munsif and sent back the case on remand for fresh trial. 

 "Where the evidence upon the record is sufficient to enable the appellate Court to pronounce judgment the appellate Court may, after resettling the issues, if necessary, finally determine the suit, notwithstanding the judgment of the Court from whose decree the appeal is preferred has proceeded wholly upon some ground other than that on which the appellate Court proceeds". 

 8. On perusal of the judgment and decree of the trial court it appears, as many as 6 P.Ws. on behalf of the plaintiff and 6 D.Ws. on behalf of defendants were examined and number of documents were filed from both sides which were marked exhibits and the learned Munsif in his own way, after proper consideration of both oral and documentary evidence, decreed the suit.
